blocks.text: Tetracycline is an antibiotic derived from soil bacteria of the genus Streptomyces. It is a bacteriostatic oral antibiotic used for infections such as chlamydia and syphilis, and it works by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis. It should not be taken with dairy foods or iron supplements. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and sensitivity to sunlight.

items: Bacteriostatic: it stops bacteria growing and multiplying rather than killing them outright.
It acts against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
It enters bacterial cells and binds reversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit.
Bound there, it stops aminoacyl-tRNA from binding to the acceptor (A) site, so translation and protein synthesis stop.
